frequency_question: How often do major banking regulatory authorities successfully raise macroprudential buffers (such as the CCyB) above zero within a defined two-year policy window when pursuing financial stability objectives?
membership_rule: Includes instances where a major central bank or prudential regulator (e.g., Fed, Bank of England, ECB, APRA) either establishes a non-zero baseline or actively raises an existing non-zero buffer to build resilience. Excludes routine microprudential capital requirement adjustments.

cases.name: Bank of England FPC UK CCyB activation
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB increase
Federal Reserve U.S. CCyB implementation evaluation periods

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.4x)
coverage_note: 12 named episodes across G10 and advanced economies; estimated roughly 15 total relevant policy evaluation windows.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging markets with less institutionalized macroprudential frameworks.
skeleton: Global peer jurisdictions with active macroprudential mandates evaluated across post-Basel III implementation windows.
multiplier: 5 major jurisdictions observed over 3 distinct economic cycles yielding roughly 15 distinct structural policy review windows.
validity_reason: Macroprudential institutional frameworks and regulatory inertia structures evolve slowly over multi-year legislative and administrative cycles.
